SkillPointsLevel5.Name: Skill Points for Level 5 Skills
SkillPointsLevel5.Hint: Skill points required to reach level 1 of a 5-level skill. The requirement doubles for each subsequent level.

SkillPointsLevel10.Name: Skill Points for Level 10 Skills
SkillPointsLevel10.Hint: Skill points required to reach level 1 of a 10-level skill. The requirement increases by this amount for each subsequent level.

CarryWeightFormula.Name: Max Carry Weight Formula
CarryWeightFormula.Hint: Base max carry weight, before size-category scaling (Tiny 25%, Small 75%, Medium 100%, Large 150%, Huge 300%, Gigantic 1000%, Titanic unlimited). A real roll formula - reference attributes as @attributes.str.value or @attributes.str.mod, skill levels as @skills.<key> (e.g. @skills.axe), and character level as @lvl.

DurabilityEnabled.Name: Enable Durability
DurabilityEnabled.Hint: Whether Weapon/Armor/Item Durability (see the Materials and Models settings) is tracked, calculated, and shown at all. Off by default.

CalendariaDailySettlementEnabled.Name: Enable Calendaria Daily Settlement
CalendariaDailySettlementEnabled.Hint: Whether Summoning and Mana Capacity/Mana Regeneration FP settle automatically on every real calendar day change (requires the "Calendaria" module to be installed and active), instead of only at the next manually confirmed Anpassungs-/Genesungspause. Still only grants pending FP, not real skill points - a Pause is still needed to integrate it. Has no effect without Calendaria. Off by default.

GeneralSettings.Name: General Settings
GeneralSettings.Hint: Skill point costs for Level 10/Level 5 skills, the max carry weight formula, whether Durability is enabled, and the optional Calendaria daily settlement.
GeneralSettings.Label: Configure General Settings

Materials.Name: Materials
Materials.Hint: Materials selectable on Items/Armor/Weapons. Material Bonus and Mana Capacity may each be a number, or "?" to let each item using this material set its own value instead.
Materials.Label: Configure Materials

Models.Name: Models
Models.Hint: Weapon Models (by weapon type) and Armor Models (Light Armor, Heavy Armor, Shield) selectable on Weapons/Armor.
Models.Label: Configure Models

Resources.Name: Resources
Resources.Hint: Define frequently used resources (e.g. Void, Faith, Yin/Yang) once. Classes, Species and Talents grant them in their GM tab; the character then gets them automatically with name, abbreviation, maximum and recovery.
Resources.Label: Configure resources

StatusEffects.Name: Status Effects
StatusEffects.Hint: Status effects selectable/toggleable on tokens and actors. Predefined ones (Exhaustion, Dazed, the four Poisoning severities) carry their own automated mechanics and can't be removed, only re-named/re-iconned/re-described; custom ones you add are flavor-only.
StatusEffects.Label: Configure Status Effects

TrainingMethods.Name: Training Methods
TrainingMethods.Hint: Training methods Characters can use (via the sheet header's Training button) to generate pending FP for a main skill and any number of secondary skills, per hour spent training.
TrainingMethods.Label: Configure Training Methods

CombatStyles.Name: Combat Styles
CombatStyles.Hint: The named Kampfstile (combat/technique styles) Technique items can belong to - see the Technique item sheet's own Style field.
CombatStyles.Label: Configure Combat Styles

ExportImport.Name: Export/Import Settings
ExportImport.Hint: Export this world's SKSK settings (skill point costs, carry weight formula, Materials, Models, Status Effects, Training Methods, Skill Usage FP, Combat Styles, Lehren) to a JSON file, or import them from one - e.g. to back up a world's configuration or copy it to another world.
ExportImport.Label: Export/Import Settings
ExportImport.ImportHint: Importing overwrites the current values of any setting present in the chosen file. Settings not present in the file are left untouched.
ExportImport.InvalidFile: That file isn't a valid SKSK settings export.
ExportImport.NothingToImport: The chosen file contains none of this system's settings.
ExportImport.ImportConfirmContent: This will overwrite {count} setting(s) with the values from the chosen file. This cannot be undone. Continue?

SkillUsageFp.Name: Skill Usage FP
SkillUsageFp.Hint: How many FP a Character generates for using a skill (skill checks, weapon attacks, spells cast, attribute rolls, ...) - Characters only, per skill category.
SkillUsageFp.Label: Configure Skill Usage FP

SkillRollApCost.Name: AP Cost: Skill/Attribute Rolls
SkillRollApCost.Hint: How much AP (on the actor's own turn) or RP (off it) rolling a skill or a raw attribute in Combat costs - split by skill (and its own usage options) and by attribute. 2 by default, always free outside of Combat.
SkillRollApCost.Label: Configure Roll AP Costs

Lehren.Name: Lehren
Lehren.Hint: The catalog of Lehren (Lore) available per skill - each Character freely distributes a shared pool of 5 levels across one skill's own Lehren, gated per-Lehre by its own minimum skill level.
Lehren.Label: Configure Lehren

EffectKeyReference.Name: Effect Key Reference
EffectKeyReference.Hint: A searchable list of every real Foundry Active Effect "Attribute Key" this system supports.
EffectKeyReference.Label: Browse Effect Keys

Deities.Name: Deities
Deities.Hint: The Deities (Patrons) actors can choose as their patron in the Religion window - with elements, Patron skills, combined magic school, domains, deeds, and numbered Patron abilities.
Deities.Label: Configure Deities

Movement.UnlockedHint: Grants access to this movement type at all, floored to a minimum speed based on the actor's size category (higher for Flying/Hovering on small creatures).

General.InspirationDieHint: Click to roll (and consume) the Inspiration die you're currently holding, once someone has granted you one.
General.NoFavoriteSkills: No favorite skills yet - star one in the Skills tab.
General.AbbreviationHint: Up to 4 letters. Usable in roll formulas as @<abbreviation>, e.g. @rage.
General.ManaAlternativeEnableHint: This resource can be spent instead of Mana - selectable via the Shift+Click menu on spell rolls. If it doesn't cover the full cost, the remainder is paid normally with Mana.
General.ManaAlternativeSpellLevelHint: 1 resource point is worth one spell level (up to 10 points at once, for a level 10 spell). Spells only.

Items.HeldOneHandedHint: A two-handed weapon is normally held with both hands, a flexible one can be switched freely. Held one-handed, Specialized loses its effect; a flexible weapon then uses its Model's one-handed roll formula.
Items.BarrierHint: Barrier this item grants when used: the formula is rolled, the card button gives it to the chosen target. Not stackable unless stated explicitly. Empty formula = no Barrier.

Longevity.ResetHint: Resets current Longevity to 100% of base Longevity (main Species including current Sub-Species multipliers).

Materials.Name: Name
Materials.VariableHint: A non-negative number, or "?" to let each item using this material set its own value

Deity.Name: Name
Deity.AbilityCountHint: Applies to every Deity equally - each Deity has exactly this many numbered abilities, which Glaubensklassen (faith classes) can reference by ability index.

SkillFpConfig.SpellCastPerLevelOutOfCombat: FP / Spell Level Cast (Out of Combat)
SkillFpConfig.WeaponsHint: FP generated per skill check and per weapon attack (including Martial Arts) using that skill, plus per kill - once the "Apply Damage" button brings a target to 0 Life and maximum Negative Life, or manually via the "Mark Kill" button on an actor's GM tab.
SkillFpConfig.ArmorsHint: FP generated whenever the Character is the target of a weapon or Martial Arts attack evaluation (hit or miss), for every armor-category skill currently equipped (worn body armor plus Shield, if any).
SkillFpConfig.MagicSchoolsHint: FP generated per spell level whenever a Simple or Advanced spell of that magic school is cast (e.g. a rate of 1 and a level-3 spell grants 3 FP) - with separate rates depending on whether a Combat is currently active or not. The last row, "Combined Magic (general)", instead applies to every Combined-magic spell cast, regardless of its own school - the resulting total is then distributed to whichever skill(s) actually enabled the cast (a single deciding skill for an override, otherwise split across the sub-skills currently at the lowest level).
SkillFpConfig.AttributeHint: FP generated whenever the corresponding attribute's own roll (not a skill check) is made - only the 8 "Unlimited X" skills apply, one per attribute.
SkillFpConfig.ResistancesHint: FP generated whenever damage of the corresponding element is taken via the "Apply Damage" button - the only skill category that's capped, though: automatic gain can never raise a Resistance past level 3 (plus any item-granted skill bonus levels); manual level changes are unaffected.
SkillFpConfig.ProductionHint: Granted via the "Production FP" header button - the player enters an already-resolved action's quality% there (plus, for Alchemy, the number of essences processed, and for Enchanting a ritual duration in hours), which scales the rate below accordingly. Enchanting additionally grants Ritualism's own "ritualHour" FP for the entered duration. Crafting is the exception: the player additionally enters the crafted item's own material level and model level, and the rate below acts as a bonus added to both levels before they're multiplied - (materialLevel + bonus) * (modelLevel + bonus) * (quality / 100).
SkillFpConfig.RogueHint: Fallen's roll lets the player choose "Falle stellen" or "Falle entschärfen" when they use it (both automated); Fingerfertigkeit's roll likewise offers a choice between its base check, Schlossknacken and Taschendiebstahl (also automated). Assassination is automated too: Assassination Attack grants FP whenever a weapon/Martial Arts attack hits while Concealed (alongside Assassination's own bonus damage), Assassination Kill additionally if that same attack kills the defender.
SkillFpConfig.MagicHint: Concentration checks, used Meditation dice, any spell cast (Magic Control, Chant Shortening once Magic Control reaches level 1), Mana Capacity/Mana Regeneration's own daily settlement (on the next Anpassungspause+, or automatically on every calendar day - see the optional Calendaria Daily Settlement in General Settings), Mana Core's flat per-item grant, Ritualism's hours per Ritual spell cast (at least 1 hour, even under the AP unit or a sub-60-minute casting time), Overcharge used (Shift+click a spell), Source-Bound/Ether-Bound (via the header's own "Quelle" button - Source Ability Used on "Quelle aktivieren", Source Opened on "Ätherquelle öffnen", each paying its own editable AP/Mana cost, no usage limit), and Summoning (via the header's Summoning button - Summoned Creature Level on "Beschwören", Day of Summon's Existence for every still-active slot on the next Anpassungspause+, or automatically on every calendar day - see the optional Calendaria Daily Settlement in General Settings) are all automated; everything else below (enchanting hours) is not yet automated - no matching system exists yet.
SkillFpConfig.FighterHint: Regeneration dice used, combat movement, Dodge used, Reflexaktion (4+ AP spent in one turn), Adrenalin used, critical hits (incl. double crit), Brutality's bonus damage points, and Technique's own cooldown rounds (any owned Technique Item currently on cooldown, granted once per Combat round it spends there) are automated; everything else below is not yet automated.
SkillFpConfig.MiscHint: Bardic magic cast (Singing), being Concealed at the start of your own turn (Stealth), prayer via the header's Prayer button (Faith), clicks on the header's Passive Perception field (Observation), Apply Damage converting an entry into healing via the defender's own Absorption (Healer - credited to whoever caused it, scaled by the healed amount), Totem (via the header's Totem button - Totem Bond Formed on "Totem binden", Totem Used on "Totem aktivieren"), and Inspiration (via the Actions window's own Inspiration button and the header's own Inspiration Die field - credited to whoever originally granted a die once it's actually rolled, whether by its own holder or via the granter's own Right-Click self-roll) are automated; everything else below is not yet automated - no matching system exists yet.
SkillFpConfig.SpecialHint: A landed hit (Hit Correction), a defended-against attack (Defense Correction), being at 0 Life with Negative Life left at the start of your own turn (Tenacity), any generic (non-Angriffswurf) D20 roll's critical success/double critical - skill checks, saving throws, attribute checks, and a manual Restrained escape attempt prompt for Neutral/Vorteil/Nachteil every time; Restrained's own turn-start/end check, Poison's recheck, and Concentration instead use the GM tab's Background Roll Mode preset with no dialog (Luck's own "Critical Roll"/"Double Critical Roll", credited to whoever rolled it - double only from Vorteil/Nachteil, both dice critical) - Soulforce's own "Meditation Die Used in Combat" (alongside Meditation's own FP whenever a Combat is active, but only while the GM tab's own "Soulforce: FP for Meditation in Combat" switch is also on, off by default), and Massacre's own 5 GM-tab Mass Kill buttons (20/50/150/500/1500 people killed within roughly 10 minutes, a fully manual GM judgment call - each tier's own rate depends on the actor's current Massacre skill level, independently configured per tier/level combination in the Skill Usage FP settings) - are automated; everything else below is not yet automated.
SkillFpConfig.StealthRound: FP / Round Concealed at Own Turn Start
SkillFpConfig.DailyManaSpent: FP / Accumulated Amount, on the Next Anpassungspause+
SkillFpConfig.RitualHour: FP / Hour Spent on a Ritual
SkillFpConfig.EnchantingHour: FP / Hour Spent Enchanting (not yet automated)
SkillFpConfig.ChantShorteningSpellCast: FP / Any Spell Cast (once Magic Control reaches level 1)
SkillFpConfig.ReflexActionUsed: FP / Reflexaktion (4+ AP Spent in One Turn)
SkillFpConfig.CriticalBonusDamagePoint: FP / Point of Critical Bonus Damage
SkillFpConfig.ZeroLifeRound: FP / Round at 0 Life (with Negative Life left) at Own Turn Start
SkillFpConfig.MeditationUsedInCombat: FP / Meditation Die Used in Combat

SkillRollApCostConfig.Hint: AP cost (on the actor's own turn) or RP cost (off it) for rolling each skill, split by its own usage options and - for skills with more than one possible attribute (e.g. Survival) - further by whichever attribute is chosen. Default 2, always free outside of Combat. Adjustable by SKSK effects via the two modifier fields (see the Effect Key Reference).
SkillRollApCostConfig.RawAttributesHint: AP/RP cost for a direct roll on a raw attribute (clicking the attribute value/modifier in the header) - independent of rolling the matching "Unlimited X" skill above, which has its own cost.

LehrenDialog.Title: Lehren
LehrenDialog.NoLehren: No Lehren defined yet for this category's skills.
LehrenDialog.MinLevelNotMet: {skill} must be at least level {level} to invest in this Lehre.
LehrenDialog.PoolExceeded: Only {pool} Lehre levels can be invested per skill.

Life.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from Classes, Constitution, Health, Tenacity and abilities - not directly editable

NegativeLife.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from max life, minus Tenacity's multiplier unless enabled on the GM tab - not directly editable
NegativeLife.IncludeToughness: Tenacity also raises max negative life
NegativeLife.IncludeToughnessHint: Let Tenacity's multiplier also raise max negative life, instead of only max life

Mana.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from Aura, Mana Capacity, Source Bound, Mana Core and abilities - not directly editable

ActionPoints.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from a base of 3 plus Reflexes (up to level 3) and any effects - not directly editable

ReactionPoints.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from max AP and Reflexes beyond level 3 - not directly editable

ArmorClass.Computed: Automatically calculated from Base AC, Constitution, worn armor/shield and any effects - not directly editable

MagicResistance.Computed: Automatically calculated from Aura, Antimagic armor/shields and any effects - not directly editable

Definition.PerPointHint: Active while the character has the resource - like the changes of an effect. "@value" is the resource's current value (e.g. -(@value * 2) for 2 less per point).
Definition.EffectValueHint: Value (formula). @value = the resource's current value, also L, @attributes.<attribute>.mod etc.
Definition.EffectPhaseHint: Initial: before the derived values are computed (attribute modifiers are not ready yet). Final: after - needed for @attributes....mod and for computed targets like system.life.max (then type "Custom").
Definition.GrantedHint: Resources from the resource settings a character gets with this item (multiple selection with Ctrl).
Definition.RemoveConfirm: Remove the resource "{name}"? It disappears from every character that has it - with its current value.
Definition.Name: Name
Definition.AbbreviationHint: Name in formulas: @abbreviation (lowercase, no spaces), e.g. @void. Always available, 0 for characters without the resource.
Definition.MaxFormulaHint: Empty = no maximum. L = character level, @attributes.con.mod, @skills.<skill>, floor()/min()/max() etc.
Definition.IntervalHint: Every how many Abschnitte (30 minutes) of a Pause
Definition.FormulaHint: Formulas: L = character level, @attributes.<attribute>.mod/.value, @skills.<skill>, @<abbreviation> (other resources), + - * / ( ), floor(), ceil(), min(), max().

Resource.SoulPowerHint: Soulforce's own collection resource - no maximum, spent via Breakthroughs and Path Abilities, or traded back into Soulforce FP below level 5 (see the GM tab's own "Soulforce: Enable New Mechanic" switch and this row's own trade button).
Resource.SoulPowerTradeNoRate: No Soul Power trade-in rate configured yet (see the Skill Usage FP settings).
Resource.SoulPowerTradeDescription: {name} used {amount} Soul Power to generate Soulforce.

ElementalCharges.ConsumeConfirm: Consume the {school} charge? Cost: {cost} AP (in combat only).

GM.NaturalMaterialBonusHint: A flat adjustment (positive or negative) to the creature's level-based natural material bonus - a floor under worn Light/Heavy armor's own AC bonus.
GM.BaseArmorClassHint: The base of Grund-AC, before the Constitution modifier is added on top.
GM.CustomArmorClassBonusHint: A flat AC bonus (positive or negative) on top of every other AC component.
GM.CustomMagicResistanceBonusHint: A flat MR bonus (positive or negative) on top of every other MR component.
GM.ManaCostReductionPercentHint: Percentage reduction of every spell's Mana cost, on top of Magic Control/Ritualism and Items' Mana-cost reductions. Negative = surcharge. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.ManaCostReductionFlatHint: Flat deduction from every spell's Mana cost (applied before the percentage discounts). Negative = surcharge. Never lowers the cost below 1. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.RitualsUseMagicControl: Rituals also discounted by Magic Control
GM.RitualsUseMagicControlHint: Spells with the "Ritual" casting method normally only get the Ritualism discount (max. 25%) on their Mana cost. With this switch the Magic Control discount (5% per level, max. 50%) applies on top. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.CriticalHitThresholdHint: The lowest natural d20 result (on an Angriffswurf/attack roll only) that counts as a critical success. 20 by default; lowering it to e.g. 15 means 15-20 all critically hit.
GM.CriticalFailureThresholdHint: The highest natural d20 result (on an Angriffswurf/attack roll only) that counts as a critical failure. 1 by default; raising it to e.g. 5 means 1-5 all critically fail.
GM.AssassinationBonusDiceHint: Extra dice of the same size as Assassination's current skill level (see Evaluate Hit) - has no effect at level 0, which only grants a flat bonus with no dice.
GM.ManaCapacityAccumulatorHint: Real mana cost paid for spells cast since the last Anpassungs-/Genesungspause - multiplied by the Mana Capacity skillUsageFp rate and floored on the next one, then reset to 0. Not meant to be hand-edited, but visible/adjustable here if needed.
GM.ManaRegenerationAccumulatorHint: Mana actually restored (Meditation, passive regen from time/Rest) since the last Anpassungs-/Genesungspause - multiplied by the Mana Regeneration skillUsageFp rate and floored on the next one, then reset to 0. Not meant to be hand-edited, but visible/adjustable here if needed.
GM.GenericCriticalRollModeHint: Neutral/Advantage/Disadvantage preset used ONLY by fully automatic generic (non-Angriffswurf) D20 checks that trigger with no player-facing dialog - Restrained's own turn-start/end escape check, Poison's recheck, Concentration. Player-triggered generic rolls (skill checks, attribute checks, saving throws, a manual Restrained escape attempt) always prompt fresh instead and ignore this. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SummonSlotsBonusHint: A flat adjustment (positive or negative) to Summoning's own slot count (see the Summoning header button), on top of the Willpower modifier - applied before the multiplier below.
GM.SummonSlotsMultiplierHint: Multiplies (Willpower modifier + the bonus above) - floored, never below 0. 1 by default (no change).
GM.TotemSlotsBonusHint: A flat adjustment (positive or negative) to Totem's own slot count (see the Totem header button), on top of the Totem skill's own level - applied before the multiplier below.
GM.TotemSlotsMultiplierHint: Multiplies (Totem skill level + the bonus above) - floored, never below 0. 1 by default (no change).
GM.SoulforceMeditationCombatFpEnabled: Soulforce: FP for Meditation in Combat
GM.SoulforceMeditationCombatFpEnabledHint: Whether using a Meditation die while a Combat is active also grants Soulforce's own "Meditation Used in Combat" FP (still scaled by that trigger's own configured rate in the Skill Usage FP settings). Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SoulPowerResourceEnabledHint: Shows the Soul Power resource on the sidebar even before Soulforce reaches its own max level (5) - it's shown regardless once that level is reached, so this only matters earlier. Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SoulPowerMechanicEnabledHint: Unlocks the trade-in button on the Soul Power resource (only while Soulforce hasn't reached its own max level (5) yet) - converts the entire current Soul Power pool into Soulforce's own FP, at the GM-configured "Soul Power Traded" rate (see the Skill Usage FP settings). Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.ElementalChargeApCost: AP Cost to Consume an Elemental Charge
GM.ElementalChargeApCostHint: Clicking a filled charge in the bar consumes it. Set per element; 0 = free. The AP (RP off your own turn) are only spent during combat.
GM.ElementalChargesEnabledHint: Shows a bar below the Actor sheet with one round slot per point of the Willpower modifier. Every spell cast from a simple magic school fills a slot (left to right, wrapping back to the start once full) with that element's color and abbreviation. Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.EnduranceAffectsHoveringHint: The Stamina skill's percentage speed bonus applies to every movement type except Hovering by default. This switch makes it apply to Hovering speed too. Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.ImprovedMagicResistanceHint: A spell attack roll that misses this actor normally still deals half damage (rounded up) anyway - with this switch on, Magic Resistance blocks that damage entirely on a miss instead. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SilverWeaknessHint: Silvered weapons (Silvered property) deal +100% damage to this actor. Also settable on the species. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.ConcealmentBreaksOnlyOnHit: Concealment doesn't break unless the attack hits
GM.ConcealmentBreaksOnlyOnHitHint: Attacking from Concealment normally lifts it immediately regardless of hit or miss - with this switch on, Concealment stays up after a miss instead. Assassination attacks are always calculated normally either way (based on Concealment at the moment of the attack). Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.ConcealmentNeverBreaksOnAttackHint: Disables the automatic Concealment break from attacking entirely (overrides the switch above too) - Assassination attacks are always calculated normally either way. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.LifeAbsorptionOverrideHint: Controls whether life-type damage (Life Magic's healing spells) heals this creature instead of harming them. Default: heals, unless the Species carries the Undead, Elemental, or Construct creature category. Can be forced or denied per-actor here regardless.

MartialArtsAttack.Name: Name
MartialArtsAttack.None: No Martial Arts Attacks defined yet.

ManualDamage.Title: Manual Damage
ManualDamage.Hint: Enter one or more damage amounts (a flat number or a dice formula), each with its own damage element - rolled on confirm and applied to your current target (or your own character otherwise), including Resistances/Weaknesses/Immunities/Absorption. Independent of any weapon/spell roll - e.g. for environmental or narrative damage.
ManualDamage.NoEntries: No valid damage entry (formula and damage element required).

ActionsDialog.ResetLayoutConfirm: Really reset the layout? Your section layout (just for you) and this actor's entry order and hidden entries will be lost.

Action.NoFavoriteSkills: No favorite skills (star in the Skills tab).
Action.NoFavoriteSpells: No favorite spells (star in the Spells tab).
Action.AdrenalinHint: Costs no AP, but reduces Adrenalin charges by 1 and restores 1 AP. Each use rolls (lifetime uses - 1)d4 as new Max Life Damage - the first use costs no max Life yet.
Action.AdrenalinDescription: {name} uses Adrenalin, restoring 1 AP and taking Adrenalin damage.
Action.InspirationHint: Grants an Inspiration die (size based on your own Inspiration skill level) to your current target, or offers it in chat for anyone to claim if nothing is targeted - spends the AP cost above and 1 Inspiration charge either way. Shift+Click to just spend a charge without granting anything (to simulate a special ability that consumes Inspiration charges). Right-Click to spend a charge and roll the die immediately for yourself.
Action.MoveHint: The first use each Combat round is free; every further use that round costs 1 AP. Outside your own turn, moving instead costs a flat 2 RP.
Action.DodgeHint: Grants disadvantage on a number of attacks against this creature. Costs 1 AP, or a flat 2 RP outside your own turn.
Action.DodgeCount: Grants disadvantage on the next {count} attacks against this creature.
Action.FreeOutsideCombat: Used for free outside Combat (no AP/RP spent).
Action.UseRpCost: RP Cost (Use, off-turn - 0 mirrors the AP Cost)
Action.RangedReactionBlocked: Ranged weapons can't be used as a reaction outside your own turn.

GeneralResource.ChargeBonusAmountHint: For Flat, a fixed bonus to the max charges. For Multiplicative, a PERCENTAGE of the max including every flat bonus (e.g. 50 = +50%, 100 = doubled); several multiplicative entries add together. The result is rounded.

Luck.NotOwner: Only this actor's own owner can reroll this roll.

AttributeReroll.NotOwner: Only this actor's own owner can reroll this roll.
AttributeReroll.NotEnabled: Reroll for this attribute is not (or no longer) enabled.

DamageReroll.RollTwiceNote: Rolls this damage roll twice and uses the better total.
DamageReroll.RerollOnesTooltip: Reroll every 1 on this damage roll
DamageReroll.NotOwner: Only this actor's own owner can reroll this roll.
DamageReroll.NotEnabled: Reroll for this element is not (or no longer) enabled.
DamageReroll.NoOnes: No 1s on this damage roll to reroll.

Mode.RollTwiceWeapon: Roll weapon/Martial Arts damage twice (Tödliche Angriffe)
Mode.RerollOnes: Reroll 1s on a damage roll of one element (Elementexperte)

FpGainBonus.Label: FP Gain Bonuses
FpGainBonus.AllowZeroHint: Only relevant for Negative/Multiplicative: checked lets this entry's reduction bring the FP gain down to 0; unchecked floors it at 1 instead.
FpGainBonus.AmountHint: A flat FP amount for Positive/Negative. A PERCENTAGE added to/subtracted from the FP gain for Multiplicative (e.g. 100 = doubles it, 50 = +50%, -50 = halves it) - not a direct multiplication factor.

EffectKeyReference.Hint: Every real system.* path a Foundry Active Effect's own "Attribute Key" field can target on an actor. Click the copy icon, or Ctrl+Right-click a field already shown on a Character sheet (an attribute box, a resource, a skill row) to copy its own key directly. Tip: an effect's own "Value" also accepts @-formulas (e.g. "@attributes.dex.mod") to increase a value by another key's current value - with "Add"/"Override" mode this works directly for any real key listed here; for an @-formula referencing a value that's only computed later (e.g. "@attributes.dex.mod" - regardless of "Add"/"Override" or "Custom" mode), the change's own Phase (selectable directly in the effect's Changes tab) must also be set to "Final", or the reference silently resolves to 0.

Category.AttributesHint: "Base" is conventionally written only by custom Status Effects, not by an Item's own Effects tab - see Species/Talent's own attributeBonuses list for the Base tier instead.
Category.DamageReductionHint: Flat reduction of every incoming damage entry by these points (after Resistance/Weakness, never below 0). Aether (true damage) and healing are not reduced. The values add up: "all", "physical", "magical" and the single damage type.
Category.HitBonusAgainstHint: Put on the marked target (spell effect on the target): attacks against it count as that much higher against Armor Class/Magic Resistance. "all" counts for every attack, an element only for attacks dealing that damage type (the best matching value counts). With the effect duration "Until used" the next matching attack uses the marker up.
Category.RollAdvantageHint: Never forced: every effect counts +1 (advantage) or -1 (disadvantage); the dialog recommends the mode that outweighs (no recommendation on a tie). The player can always freely choose advantage/neutral/disadvantage. Enter 1 or -1 as the value (mode "Add").
Category.ExtraDamageHint: Use a number or dice formula as Value (e.g. 5, 1d6, 1d6 + @attributes.wil.mod). [element] sets a damage type (e.g. 1d6[fire] or 1d6[fire] + 1d4[cold]), otherwise the attack's own damage type applies. The extra damage is rolled for every damage instance (weapon/martial arts attack, damage entry of a spell) and applied separately (resistances etc.). All matching effects stack. Combine with the effect duration "Until used".
Category.ExtraDamageWeaponsAll: Extra damage: weapon attacks (Martial Arts halved)
Category.ExtraDamageWeapons: Extra damage: weapon attacks (without Martial Arts)
Category.ExtraDamageSchool: Extra damage: spells of the school {school}
Category.SkillLevelHint: Raises (or lowers) the skill LEVEL itself directly, e.g. "system.skillLevelBonus.waterResistance" with mode "Add" and value 5 for Water Resistance 5. Added on top of the finished level (0 to its max level), so it changes neither points nor level-up XP and suits toggleable/temporary effects. For binary skills (Absorption, Immunity, ...) any value of 1 or more unlocks them; for Weaknesses it raises the stack count.

Spell.UpkeepHint: Permanently reduces the caster's maximum mana by this amount for as long as "Sustaining" is on. Multiple active upkeep costs add up, but can never push maximum mana below 0.
Spell.UpkeepPerManaHint: Additional upkeep per Mana of the amount chosen at cast time (e.g. 3 = "3 upkeep per Mana", 0.5 = "50% of the cost"), rounded up. Added to the upkeep above.
Spell.UpkeepVariableHint: With "?" the upkeep is entered when the spell is activated ("Sustaining").
Spell.RangeDistanceHint: Metres - fractions allowed (e.g. 2.5). For "Sphere" it is the radius, for "Cuboid" the volume in m³.
Spell.SustainingHint: Marks this spell as currently active (e.g. after its normal Duration has run out and the caster keeps it going via a "can be sustained" duration) - arms Mana Cost Per Round and Upkeep.
Spell.UpkeepAutoDeactivated: {name}: No longer sustained - not enough mana for the per-round cost.
Spell.OverchargeAutoEffectsHint: When on, saving throw DC (+1), range (+20%) and damage (+50%) all scale automatically per Überladung. Turn off for a spell with a hand-written Custom Effect - the increased AP/Mana cost still applies either way, but the actual effect is then calculated manually.
Spell.OverchargeSettingsHint: How this spell reacts to Overcharges. The defaults are the general rules (+20% Mana, +1 AP, +1 DC, +20% range, +50% damage per Overcharge); 0 turns an aspect off. The "Automatic Overcharge Effects" switch above disables DC, range and damage together.
Spell.OverchargeEffectHint: Scaling: DC, range and damage rise. Extra attack: instead, every Overcharge triggers one more attack (with its damage and effects, no FP gain) - only for spells that have an attack roll anyway.
Spell.OverchargeDurationHint: Shown as an extra duration line in the chat for an overcharged spell. {n} is the number of Overcharges, simple formulas work inside braces, e.g. "{2+n} rounds".
Spell.ExtraManaCostsHint: Cumulative tiers of extra Mana cost - paying tier 2 also requires paying tier 1. Chosen via Shift+Click on the spell, in the same window as Overcharge. A Damage row can be tied to one of these tiers via the "Extra Cost" trigger.
Spell.ManaCostVariableHint: Enter "?": the Mana cost is asked every time the spell is used.
Spell.ApCostVariableHint: Enter "?" if the AP cost is chosen when casting (AP unit only). The minimum is set in the "Min. AP" field.
Spell.ApCostMinHint: Lowest AP amount that can be chosen when casting.
Spell.ApCostFixedHint: This spell's AP cost cannot be reduced (neither by abilities/effects nor by Chant Shortening). Overcharging still increases it.
Spell.RequiresInfusionWeapon: Must be cast with an Infusion weapon
Spell.RequiresInfusionWeaponHint: This spell can only be cast while the caster has an equipped weapon with the Infusion property. Also applies to abilities with an attached spell.

Variant.Hint: Variants change this spell while a marker status or effect is on the caster (e.g. the Trickery "Infusion" spells or "Gather Water"). A marker with the effect duration "Until used" is used up by the cast; with any other duration the variant applies to every cast while it is active.
Variant.Label: Variants
Variant.ChoiceHint: A variant to choose from: casting asks which of the "Chosen when casting" variants applies (they are alternatives of each other). Needs no conditions.
Variant.Name: Name
Variant.NoteHint: Free text shown on the chat card - for anything the changes or extra entries cannot express.
Variant.ConditionsHint: Markers on the caster. A status is recognised by its id, an effect by its exact name.
Variant.ChangesHint: Every option of the spell can be changed: option = path into the spell data (e.g. manaCost, apCost, duration, ranges.0.distance, damages.0.formula, savingThrows.0.baseValue). "Set" replaces, "Add"/"Multiply" calculate (Mana is rounded down afterwards), "Append" adds text.
Variant.ScopeHint: "This spell": the variant changes this spell when its conditions are met. "Next spell": an infusion - the variant is stored here but changes the next spell its caster casts (as far as it passes the filter). This spell needs a marker effect with the duration "Until used" on the caster for that; with no conditions the variant applies while this marker is present.
Variant.FilterHint: Only spells that pass every filled-in filter are changed. Separate lists with commas, empty = no restriction. Changes may address every entry of a list with "*", e.g. damages.*.formula.
Variant.ConsumeOnMismatch: Use up the marker even for a non-matching spell
Variant.ConsumeOnMismatchHint: On: "the next spell" always uses up the marker. Off: the marker stays until a matching spell is cast.

Spell.ExtraManaCostRepeatableHint: This step can be chosen several times when casting. Its Mana cost and any Extra Cost damage tied to it then count that many times.

PoisonMedium.Description: 1d6 poison damage and a Constitution check (DC 13) every 3 rounds (first triggering 3 rounds after being poisoned). A successful check cures it.

PoisonSevere.Name: Severe Poisoning
PoisonSevere.Description: 1d8 poison damage and a Constitution check (DC 16) every 5 rounds (first triggering 5 rounds after being poisoned). A successful check cures it.

PoisonDeadly.Name: Deadly Poisoning
PoisonDeadly.Description: 1d10 poison damage and a Constitution check (DC 19) every 10 rounds (first triggering 10 rounds after being poisoned). A successful check cures it.

Prone.Name: Prone
Prone.Description: Can't use weapon attacks (incl. Martial Arts Attacks) or cast spells with the Movement casting method. Can still move.

Restrained.Name: Restrained
Restrained.Description: Can't move, use weapon attacks (incl. Martial Arts Attacks), or cast spells with the Movement casting method. Carries its own escape check difficulty and timing (an AP cost spendable any time, or an automatic check at the start/end of its own Combat turn) - a passed Strength check removes it entirely.

Frostbite.Name: Frostbite
Frostbite.Description: Stackable, capped at (Constitution modifier + 4) - a stack beyond the cap applies 1 Dazed stack instead. Deals flat Cold damage (2x the first Class's Life value, plus the second Class's once unlocked) at the start of each round of the creature's turn, regardless of its own stack count.

Wound.Name: Wound
Wound.Description: Every time a Wound is suffered, its damage is rolled (1d[life value of the first Class] + 1d[life value of the second Class]) and added to the Wound value. At the start of the creature's turn, it suffers the whole Wound value.

MaxLifeDamage.Name: Max Life Damage
MaxLifeDamage.Description: Can be suffered multiple times, from different sources - each instance permanently reduces max Life by its own value (and max Negative Life too, once Tenacity's buffer is exhausted).

Cauterization.Name: Cauterization
Cauterization.Description: Comes with a value that reduces max Life (like Max Life Damage, and Negative Life too once Tenacity's buffer is exhausted). A second application doesn't stack separately - it merges into the existing value instead.

AdrenalinDamage.Name: Adrenalin Damage
AdrenalinDamage.Description: Comes with a value that reduces max Life (like Max Life Damage/Cauterization, and Negative Life too once Tenacity's buffer is exhausted), caused specifically by Adrenalin's own escalating damage. A second application doesn't stack separately - it merges into the existing value instead. Reduced (not fully healed) by Anpassungspause (Constitution modifier) or Genesungspause (whichever is higher between Character level and Constitution modifier) - Adrenalin's separate used count, which drives future rolls, resets to 0 at any qualifying Pause instead.

Charmed.Name: Charmed
Charmed.Description: This creature has been charmed by another creature. It can't attack the source of this status effect, nor target it with negative spells or other negative effects. The source of this status effect has advantage on all rolls resulting from a social interaction with this creature.

Feared.Name: Fear
Feared.Description: This creature is in a state of panicked fear of something or someone. It can't voluntarily move closer to the source of this status effect, and suffers disadvantage on all rolls while it can see, hear, or otherwise perceive the source.

Petrified.Name: Petrified
Petrified.Description: This creature has been petrified. While this status effect applies, this creature and everything it's carrying turns to magical stone. While petrified, its weight increases tenfold and it stops aging. It is completely immobile, can't speak, and perceives nothing of its surroundings. It is immune to Poison damage and Poisoning; if it was already poisoned before this status effect took effect, the poisoning isn't cured, only paused. Should this creature be forced to make Strength, Dexterity, sight-based Perception, or Charisma checks, they automatically fail (this doesn't count as a critical failure). This creature takes halved damage from all sources except Aether, Earth, and Blunt damage while petrified, and attacks against it are always made with advantage.

Blind.Name: Blind
Blind.Description: This creature is blind in at least one eye. If blind in only one eye, it has disadvantage on Perception checks and attack rolls. If completely blind, sight-based Perception checks and ranged attacks automatically fail; melee attacks still only have disadvantage.

Concentration.Name: Concentration
Concentration.Description: This creature is concentrating on a task. If it takes damage, it must pass a Concentration check (1d20 + Constitution modifier + Concentration skill level) against a DC of (damage / 2, minimum 5), or its concentration breaks (this status effect is removed). Multiple "damage at the start of the turn" sources are summed together and checked only once per round.

Concealed.Name: Concealed
Concealed.Description: This creature is concealed/hidden in combat. While active, it generates Stealth's own pending FP (if configured) at the start of each of its own Combat turns.

ActiveManaCore.Name: Active Mana Core
ActiveManaCore.Description: Increases both maximum and current Mana by (Mana Core skill level * 50) and activates Concentration. If Concentration breaks, this status is automatically removed - any excess Mana (above the maximum without this effect) is lost in the process.

Models.Name: Name
Models.TwoHandedDiceFormulaHint: Only for weapons with Flexible: roll formula while the weapon is held two-handed (the normal roll formula applies one-handed). Empty: same formula.
Models.DistantAttributesHint: Optional: attributes an attack over more than 2m (attack and damage roll) is calculated with instead of the normal ones.
Models.AttributeOverrideHint: This weapon's Angriffswurf (attack roll) attribute bonus normally draws from its Model's own Attribute Modifiers Used. Enable this for a unique variant of that Model that should use different attributes instead.
Models.DamageTypeOverrideHint: This weapon's damage type (for Resistance/Weakness/Immunity/Absorption purposes) normally draws from its Model's own Damage Type. Enable this for a unique variant of that Model that should deal a different damage type instead.
Models.DurabilityMultiplierOverrideHint: This item's max Durability normally multiplies its Material's own base value by its Model's own Durability Multiplier (always 1 for items with no Model). Enable this to override that multiplier for this specific item instead.
Models.QualityHint: 100 = normal. Multiplicatively scales (rounded down) this item's own combined Material+Model flat attack/damage bonus (Weapon) or AC/MR bonus (Armor) - the wielder's own skill/attribute/Lehren contributions are never affected.

Heavy.Name: Heavy
Heavy.Hint: This item is heavy and requires a Strength score of at least the given requirement to use effectively. Below it, all attribute and skill bonuses of the wielder for this item are lost (the Material bonus stays). A two-handed weapon with this modifier can only be held one-handed with Strength of at least X + 25% of X (rounded up).

Demanding.Name: Demanding
Demanding.Hint: This item is hard to handle and requires a Dexterity score of at least the given requirement to use effectively. Below it, all attribute and skill bonuses of the wielder for this item are lost (the Material bonus stays). A two-handed weapon with this modifier can only be held one-handed with Dexterity of at least X + 25% of X (rounded up).

Draining.Name: Draining
Draining.Hint: Using this item tires the bearer quickly and requires a Constitution score of at least the given requirement to use effectively. Below it, all attribute and skill bonuses of the wielder for this item are lost (the Material bonus stays). A two-handed weapon with this modifier can only be held one-handed with Constitution of at least X + 25% of X (rounded up).

Refined.Name: Refined
Refined.Hint: This weapon uses one of its listed attributes (user's choice). Incompatible with Specialized and Masterful.

Specialized.Name: Specialized
Specialized.Hint: This weapon uses its listed attribute twice. Incompatible with Simple, Refined and Masterful. If combined with the Two-Handed modifier, this modifier loses its effect unless the weapon is wielded two-handed.

Masterful.Name: Masterful
Masterful.Hint: This item is far better in the hands of someone who has mastered two attributes. Such an item uses two attributes - the higher of the two is used, and if both are equal, both are used. Incompatible with Simple, Refined and Specialized.

Rending.Name: Rending
Rending.Hint: A weapon with this modifier deals double damage to constructs, material undead, objects (creature category Object) and inorganic obstacles. Buildings are not implemented yet.

Stunning.Name: Stunning
Stunning.Hint: A critical attack with a weapon with this modifier gives the target several stacks of Dazed. The amount is the Material bonus / 2, multiplied by (X/10) if the weapon has the Heavy (X) modifier.

Disarming.Name: Disarming
Disarming.Hint: A creature using an item with this modifier can try, as a reaction (3 RP) to a melee weapon attack, to disarm the attacker. They must pass a DC 16 Dexterity or DC 18 Strength check (attacker's choice) and are disarmed on a failure, the weapon is unequipped. The attack then fails.

Ranged.Name: Ranged
Ranged.Hint: A weapon with this modifier can attack at range (given in brackets / disadvantage at extended range, not automatic). In direct combat, i.e. 2m or less from the targeted target, such a weapon cannot be used to attack.

Reload.Name: Reload
Reload.Hint: After a weapon with this modifier has been used for Magazine Size attack rolls (Magazine Size 1 if unset), it must be reloaded before it can attack again. Pressing the weapon attack button again instead reloads it for the given Action Points, without attacking.

Flexible.Name: Flexible
Flexible.Hint: A weapon with this modifier can be held one-handed or two-handed at any time (switch in the Actions window/inventory). Its Model can have a separate two-handed roll formula. Bows cannot be held one-handed.

Shapeshifting.Name: Shapeshifting
Shapeshifting.Hint: This item can change its form. A weapon can turn into another one or even an armor piece. The overall mass of the item cannot change through this modifier. Costs 3 action points (button "Use Shapeshifting" in the Actions window, the GM switches the item).

Infusion.Name: Infusion
Infusion.Hint: This weapon can be charged with mana and used for the abilities Magic Attacks and Deadly Attacks. Spells with the switch "Must be cast with an Infusion weapon" can only be cast with an equipped Infusion weapon. If this effect is natural on a material, it is lost when the weapon is enchanted (except with this modifier). Antimagic items with this modifier can be enchanted or reinforced with magic.

Unstable.Name: Unstable
Unstable.Hint: An item with this modifier is unstable. A d10 is rolled every round; on a 10 the item takes another form by itself - the GM decides which. This modifier can only be applied to items with the Shapeshifting modifier or the Form-Adapting enchantment.

Long.Name: Long
Long.Hint: A weapon with this modifier has double melee reach. Optionally attributes can be set that attack and damage rolls over more than 2m use instead of the normal ones (mostly for the overrides on the item).

Light.Name: Light
Light.Hint: A weapon with this modifier is (X*5%) lighter than normal without getting weaker. Heavy armor with this modifier gives no disadvantage on stealth rolls if X is at least 6.

Antimagic.Name: Antimagic
Antimagic.Hint: An item with this modifier cannot be enchanted, deals double damage to Barriers (magic shields) and ignores AC bonuses the target has from spells. The attacked creature also has disadvantage on its Concentration check. Armor made of materials with this modifier grants Magic Resistance equal to (armor AC / 2, rounded down).

Reach.Name: Reach
Reach.Hint: A weapon with this modifier can attack at range (given in brackets). Over more than 2m, attack and damage rolls use the attributes set here (the normal ones if none are set).

GiantSlayer.Name: Giant Slayer
GiantSlayer.Hint: Large-sized creatures take 25% extra damage, Gigantic-sized creatures take 50% extra damage, Titanic-sized creatures take 100% extra damage.

VeryLong.Name: Very Long
VeryLong.Hint: A weapon with this modifier has triple melee reach. Optionally attributes can be set that attack and damage rolls over more than 2m use instead of the normal ones (mostly for the overrides on the item).

Simple.Name: Simple
Simple.Hint: A weapon or armor with this modifier can be used effectively even without the corresponding skill. At the same time, it gains no bonus from skills (though skill points for the corresponding skill can still be earned). Incompatible with Specialized, Masterful and Refined.

Redirection.Name: Redirection
Redirection.Hint: The bearer of an item with this modifier can, as a reaction (3 RP), redirect an attack without an area effect to the nearest creature within 2m, unless that creature passes a DC 15 Constitution check. The new target gets a new attack roll against AC or MR. Spell attacks can only be redirected if the item is enchanted.

Silvered.Name: Silvered
Silvered.Hint: Weapons of this material deal +100% damage to creatures weak to silver (switch on the actor or the species).

Concealed.Name: Concealed
Concealed.Hint: An attack with this weapon does not automatically remove Concealment. Creatures hit by an attack with such a weapon gain advantage on their next Perception roll to uncover the attacker (only a recommendation in chat).

Wounding.Name: Wounding
Wounding.Hint: A successful attack with this weapon automatically inflicts a Wound.

Throwable.Name: Throwable
Throwable.Hint: This item can be thrown (no penalty on weapon attacks). A weapon enchanted with this modifier returns after the attack.

Shattering.Name: Shattering
Shattering.Hint: Attacks with a weapon with this modifier deal five times the durability damage to the armor / shield of the attacked target or to the weapon used to parry.

TwoHanded.Name: Two-Handed
TwoHanded.Hint: A weapon with this modifier is wielded with both hands. One-handed only works with the switch in the Actions window/inventory and only if the bearer has the attributes: with Heavy/Demanding/Draining (X) at least X + 25% of X (rounded up) in that attribute, otherwise at least 16 in the attribute the weapon uses. Held one-handed, Specialized loses its effect. Bows cannot be held one-handed.

Deployable.Name: Deployable
Deployable.Hint: A shield with this modifier can be deployed, after which it counts as an inorganic obstacle providing full or half cover.

ArmBound.Name: Arm-Bound
ArmBound.Hint: A shield with this modifier can't be lost unless the bearing arm is severed. Additionally, the hand of the arm wielding this shield can still be used for attacks.

Hardened.Name: Hardened (X)
Hardened.Hint: This item is hardened and grants AC increased by X (maximum is Material Bonus / 2).

Loud.Name: Loud
Loud.Hint: The wearer should have disadvantage on stealth rolls while wearing this item (only a recommendation in chat - whether it applies depends on the situation).

Reflective.Name: Reflective
Reflective.Hint: Reflects 10% of the magical damage its bearer takes back onto the source.

Flawless.Name: Flawless
Flawless.Hint: A critical attack roll made against the bearer of an item with this modifier still hits automatically, but deals no extra damage.

Spiky.Name: Spiky
Spiky.Hint: Creatures that attack the wearer of such an item with a melee weapon attack suffer the given piercing damage (formula, 1d6 if blank).

ItemSheet.ManaCoreFpGrantHint: Flat FP granted to the Manakern skill each time this is used - a designer-set value on this item itself, not a GM-configured rate.
ItemSheet.AllowBelowOneHint: This entry's flat reduction can push the cost below 1 (down to 0).
ItemSheet.ChargesDepleted: {actor} uses 1 charge. All of this item's charges are used up.
